subject: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners

Ethan/Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned as we scope the short POC: 

Top-level goal
- Validate that Redwood Inference can meet the latency and cost profile for your realtime summarization pipeline while preserving output precision for the clinical note extraction use case.

Proposed evaluation pillars (P95 target & ownership):
- Latency (P95): <= 200 ms — owner: Nimbus infra (observability) + Redwood eng (runtime config)
- Throughput: sustained 80–120 qps for 512-token requests — owner: Nimbus infra for load shaping; Redwood to validate scaling behavior
- Cost per effective token: target <= $0.0008/token (model + infra amortized) — owner: joint (finance + Redwood solutions)
- Quality: automated pass rate >= 85% on internal validation set (precision-focused) and spot human review for edge cases — owner: Nimbus ML

Deliverables we propose for the two-week trial:
1) Smoke validation (3 days): functional correctness and sample throughput/latency sweep using your sample payloads.
2) Stability run (7 days): sustained load at target qps, observe autoscaling behavior and tail latency.
3) Quality audit (running): evaluate against your labeled set and random human checks.

Owners and points of contact:
- Nimbus: Ethan (technical lead), Priya (product/clinical), Jared (cloud ops)
- Redwood: Kimberly (deal lead), Marcus (service performance), Lauren (customer success)

Immediate asks (this week)
- Ethan: share a pipelined sample of 200 representative requests + 2k labeled examples (we can start with a subset). Prefer S3 link or one of the attached payload examples.
- Priya: confirm the quality metric definition (what constitutes a pass on the 85% metric) — we can adapt if you want F1/precision thresholds.
- Nimbus infra: confirm IP allowlist and target VPC subnet for private trial (if required).

I attached a short smoke_test_checklist.xlsx and a sample payload bundle to make the first run frictionless.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday to walk through the smoke steps unless you prefer a different cadence.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: smoke_test_checklist.xlsx (stub), nimbus_poc_payload_examples.json (stub)

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbushealth.com>, Jared Milton <jared@cloudops.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners

Kimberly —

Appreciate the summary and very clear plan. Priya and I talked internally and this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Quality metric: we want precision >= 90% on the named-entity extraction (clinical entities) subset and recall >= 80% on the summary extraction subset; overall pass rate of 85% is fine as a contract-level goal but we'll evaluate both submetrics.
- Latency: 200 ms P95 is a hard requirement for interactive triage workflows; for batched offline jobs we can accept higher tail latencies.
- Cost: the $0.0008/token is a target — if we can show clear scaling tradeoffs (e.g., quantized variant at lower cost with minor quality delta) we'll consider follow-on procurement.

I've uploaded an initial 300-sample packet and the 2k labeled examples to our S3 and shared the link via the DocSend blob in related links. Jared will also follow up with networking details for the private trial.

We can do the Monday kickoff; 10:00am PT works for Priya/Ethan.

Thanks,
Ethan
CTO, Nimbus Health

Attachments referenced: s3://nimbus-poc/samples/20261126_bundle.zip

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners

Ethan —

Quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff:
- For the 512-token scenario you'll get best P95 by enabling prefix KV cache and setting batch windows to 10–20ms; we'll propose an initial runtime profile for the smoke run.
- We'll run two model variants in parallel: standard float model (higher quality) and an int8 quantized variant for cost comparison. We'll log per-token compute usage so we can reconcile to your finance model.
- Throughput: to reach 100 qps we expect to need 4 modest GPUs for the initial burst profile with our current config — we will test autoscaling thresholds during the stability run.
- Instrumentation: please make sure your sample requests include a stable request_id header so we can correlate logs to your labeled examples.

I'll drop a brief CSV template for latency/throughput logging (attached) and a sample command line for the smoke run.

—Marcus
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_latency-throughput-template.csv (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. I'll capture this as the official POC charter and owners so procurement and engineering have something to reference. Summary additions: 

- Kickoff: Mon 2026-11-30 10:00 PT — Zoom invite to follow.
- Smoke run (Owner: Redwood eng / Marcus): 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-02 — functional and latency sweep. 
- Stability run (Owner: Nimbus infra + Redwood ops): 2026-12-03 to 2026-12-10 — sustained load and autoscale behavior.
- Quality audit (Owner: Nimbus ML + Redwood SE / Lauren): ongoing, initial report by 2026-12-07.
- Acceptance gates: pass quality submetrics (precision >= 90% entity; recall >= 80% summary) AND P95 latency <= 200ms on interactive profile. Cost target is advisory for this run.

Action items now: 
- Ethan: confirm S3 link and provide IAM read token for the sample set (if you prefer a different transfer method say so).
- Priya: confirm that the precision/recall thresholds above match your expectations — if you'd rather use a single composite metric we'll accept that but prefer the two-submetric evaluation.
- Jared: share network allowlist info and whether you prefer a hosted-hosted trial or a VPC-to-VPC private test.

I'll attach the POC charter PDF after the kickoff; for now the smoke checklist and sample payloads are attached.

Best,
Kimberly

Attachments: smoke_test_checklist.xlsx, nimbus_poc_payload_examples.json

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>, Jared Milton <jared@cloudops.io>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health trial — validation metrics & owners

Kimberly/Marcus —

Looks good to me. Confirming:
- We hold to precision >= 90% (entity) and recall >= 80% (summary) as initial quality gates.
- We'll prioritize interactive profile for latency gating; offline/batch can have separate acceptance criteria.
- IAM token and S3 link sent to your inbox (Ethan forwarded) and Jared will confirm network plan tomorrow.

See you Mon 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Priya
Product Lead, Clinical AI
Nimbus Health
